source_disagreements: Large Bandwidth Tunnel requirements (VPNTunnels) say 'MTU limit remains 1500 bytes'; vpn-limits says 1446 bytes (MSS 1406). Only the vpn-limits value is stored.
VPN Concentrator quota row says 'per Transit Gateway or Cloud WAN'; the vpn-concentrator page says Concentrators are only supported with Transit Gateway, not Cloud WAN. Both are stored with a note.

Client VPN: best-practices says a maximum baseline bandwidth of 50 Mbps per user connection; test-throughput says a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps is supported per user connection. Both stored as separate facts.

Client VPN history: row 2024-12-19 says authorization rules 50 to 100 and routes 10 to 100; row 2025-03-13 says authorization rules 50 to 200; the What's New post of 2025-03-18 says 10 to 100 routes and 50 to 200 rules. The current default is 200 and 100.

Direct Connect FAQ (answers 90 and 91) still says you can advertise up to 100 routes over each BGP session, without naming a virtual interface type; the quotas page says 100 by default on private or transit (up to 1,000 with prefix controls) and 1,000 on public.

Direct Connect SLA page (updated 2026-07-24) names the deployments Multi-Site Redundant and Multi-Site Non-Redundant; connection_options and the Resiliency Toolkit still say Maximum Resiliency (99.99%) and High Resiliency (99.9%).

The aws.amazon.com Direct Connect resiliency-recommendation page still says VPN is not recommended as backup for connections faster than 1 Gbps and that ECMP over transit gateway reaches up to 50 Gbps; the 2025 Large Bandwidth Tunnel pages recommend 5 Gbps VPN as backup for 10 Gbps+ circuits. Decisions lens: prefer the guide pages.

Dedicated connections quota rows 1 and 2: transit virtual interfaces per connection (4) say 'Contact your Solutions Architect or Technical Account Manager', while the combined total (51) says 'This limit cannot be increased'.
